title: Emergency surgical cricothyroidotomy on a manikin

guidelineVersions: Difficult Airway Society (DAS), 2025 adult difficult tracheal intubation guidelines, published in BJA 2026; accessed 12 October 2026

brief.scenario: You are the core surgical trainee assisting the anaesthetic team in theatre. An adult manikin represents a patient who cannot be intubated or oxygenated despite failed intubation, supraglottic airway and two-person mask ventilation. The consultant anaesthetist announces “CICO; proceed to emergency front-of-neck airway (eFONA).” An anaesthetist remains at the head providing oxygenation attempts and calling for help.
brief.task: Demonstrate on the training manikin how you would prepare and perform a scalpel–bougie–tube emergency cricothyroidotomy, explaining your actions. 9 minutes; 1 minute reading.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: This tests recognition of CICO as an oxygenation emergency, decisive transition to Plan D, disciplined scalpel–bougie–tube technique, and confirmation of effective ventilation on a manikin.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Persisting with repeated upper-airway attempts after CICO has been declared, or declaring success without waveform capnography.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: “CICO confirmed. I am proceeding with emergency front-of-neck airway now. Please continue oxygen delivery, call for help and bring the eFONA kit.”

flow: Declare CICO, allocate roles, and continue oxygen delivery while preparing Plan D.
Identify laryngeal anatomy; position and stabilise the larynx; select the appropriate vertical-incision approach when landmarks are uncertain.
Perform the taught scalpel entry, identify the membrane/opening, place bougie and railroad a suitable cuffed tracheal tube.
Inflate cuff, connect breathing circuit, confirm ventilation with sustained waveform capnography and chest movement.
Secure tube, document procedure, arrange definitive airway/critical-care follow-up and check for complications.

grid.label: Recognition and declaration
grid.fail: Does not accept CICO; continues failed upper airway attempts
grid.borderline: Names difficulty without committing to Plan D
grid.pass: Declares CICO and immediate Plan D
grid.high: Declares CICO decisively and delegates simultaneous oxygenation/help

grid.label: Team and equipment
grid.borderline: Requests help but omits key equipment
grid.pass: Calls senior help, assigns oxygenation, requests scalpel, bougie and cuffed tube
grid.high: Uses closed-loop role assignment and checks equipment readiness

grid.label: Anatomy and position
grid.borderline: Finds approximate site but insecure stabilisation
grid.pass: Identifies thyroid/cricoid cartilages and membrane; stabilises larynx
grid.high: Adapts method to impalpable anatomy without dangerous repeated probing

grid.label: Skin and membrane access
grid.borderline: Access sequence hesitant or poorly controlled
grid.pass: Uses trained vertical skin approach when required and controlled membrane access
grid.high: Explains why incision approach changes when landmarks are unclear

grid.label: Bougie placement
grid.pass: Introduces bougie into tracheal lumen under controlled conditions
grid.high: Stabilises access and avoids false passage or excessive force

grid.label: Tube placement
grid.fail: Tube not railroaded or unsecured during placement
grid.borderline: Tube placed but cuff/circuit step incomplete
grid.pass: Railroads cuffed tube over bougie, removes bougie, inflates cuff and connects circuit
grid.high: Coordinates tube passage and assistants to minimise loss of airway

grid.label: Confirm ventilation
grid.borderline: Mentions only chest rise or auscultation
grid.pass: Uses sustained waveform capnography and clinical ventilation signs
grid.high: Recognises absent trace as possible wrong placement and immediately troubleshoots

grid.label: Safety and escalation
grid.borderline: Calls help late or provides limited postprocedure plan
grid.pass: Continues oxygen delivery, escalates and anticipates bleeding/trauma
grid.high: Explains rescue if tube ineffective and leads postprocedure re-evaluation

grid.label: Handover and documentation
grid.pass: Secures tube, states critical-care handover, records attempts and complications
grid.high: Provides succinct structured handover and early definitive review

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: This is a cannot-intubate, cannot-oxygenate emergency. Plan D is required.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will try laryngoscopy once more; perhaps the view will improve.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The anaesthetist confirms that rescue approaches have failed and oxygenation is worsening.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I do not need to call anyone yet. I have a scalpel.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I cannot feel the membrane clearly, but I will cut roughly where I think it is.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The membrane is difficult to feel.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will stab directly without exposing the landmarks.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: A tract is made on the model. What next?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I push the bougie until it stops.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I put the tube over it but have not checked the cuff or connections.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: There is no sustained end-tidal CO₂ trace.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The tube is probably right because it went in. We can finish.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What will you do after the procedure?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I will leave the team to sort out the rest.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: This is a cannot-intubate, cannot-oxygenate emergency. Plan D is required.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I accept CICO. I am proceeding to emergency front-of-neck airway immediately; no further repeated laryngoscopy.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Please call the consultant anaesthetist and bring the eFONA kit. Continue oxygen delivery at the head of the patient. I need a scalpel, bougie, cuffed tube, syringe and breathing circuit.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: They are available. Show me the preparation.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I check and expose the front of the neck, position the head as feasible and stabilise the larynx. I identify thyroid cartilage, cricoid cartilage and the cricothyroid membrane.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The membrane is difficult to feel.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I will not make a blind stab at an uncertain point. I stabilise the larynx and use the DAS vertical skin incision approach to expose and identify the membrane.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I demonstrate a controlled vertical skin incision on the model, bluntly identify the membrane and enter it with the scalpel according to the taught technique.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The opening is demonstrated. What next?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I maintain access and pass the bougie into the trachea without force.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I railroad the appropriately sized cuffed tube over the bougie, remove the bougie, inflate the cuff and attach the breathing circuit.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: There is no sustained end-tidal CO₂ trace.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: That is not confirmed ventilation. I immediately check the circuit, tube position and patency with the airway team; I do not assume the tube is intratracheal.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: After correcting a disconnected sampling line, a persistent capnography waveform appears with chest movement.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Now we have sustained waveform capnography and chest movement confirming effective ventilation. I will continue monitoring.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Please assess for bleeding, subcutaneous emphysema and tube displacement, and arrange urgent senior airway and critical-care review.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I secure the tube, document the time and reason for Plan D, technique, confirmation and complications, and hand over to the anaesthetic and critical-care teams.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: This is a cannot-intubate, cannot-oxygenate emergency. Plan D is required.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: CICO confirmed. Stop further upper-airway instrumentation and activate Plan D. We cannot afford a delay while oxygenation is failing.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Anaesthetist, please keep oxygen delivery going. Assistant one, call additional skilled help and announce CICO. Assistant two, check the eFONA kit: scalpel, bougie, cuffed tube, syringe and breathing circuit. Tell me when ready.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The kit and help are ready.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I expose the neck and palpate the thyroid cartilage, cricoid cartilage and interposed membrane while firmly stabilising the larynx. I assess whether the landmarks are reliably palpable before deciding skin access.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The membrane is difficult to feel.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I will use a generous vertical midline skin incision to expose the laryngeal structures rather than repeatedly puncturing an uncertain landmark; I keep control of the larynx.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: On the trainer, I incise the skin, separate tissue in the midline, identify the membrane and create a controlled opening with the scalpel in the recommended sequence.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Keeping the scalpel opening oriented and the larynx stabilised, I advance the bougie gently into the tracheal lumen; if resistance suggests a false passage I stop and reassess.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I advance a cuffed tracheal tube over the bougie, maintain bougie control, withdraw it, inflate the cuff, connect the circuit and request ventilation.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: There is no sustained end-tidal CO₂ trace.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: We have not proved ventilation. Stop labelling this successful. Check patient connection, sampling line and tube position now; if capnography remains absent I must suspect ineffective or misplaced access and restore oxygenation urgently with senior assistance.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The capnography sampling line was disconnected; after reconnection a sustained waveform and chest movement are seen.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A sustained waveform now confirms ventilation, supported by bilateral chest movement and improving physiology. Maintain continuous capnography.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would anticipate bleeding and surgical emphysema, reassess oxygenation and tube security, and plan definitive airway management with the consultant.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I secure the tube and give a structured handover: CICO after failed Plans A–C, Plan D technique, tube placement and capnography confirmation, any complications, and required ICU monitoring.

failures.move: Continuing repeated intubation attempts after CICO is declared.
Blind uncontrolled incision at an uncertain location.
failures.consequence: Risks major injury and failed airway.
Risks false passage or traumatic injury.

failures.move: Accepting unconfirmed placement despite absent waveform capnography.
Failing to summon help or maintain oxygenation efforts.

recovery.when: If you have lost the landmark
recovery.line: I have lost the landmark; I will stabilise the larynx, use the vertical exposure approach and re-identify the membrane.

recovery.when: If there is no waveform capnography
recovery.line: There is no waveform capnography; ventilation is not confirmed. I need to troubleshoot and restore oxygenation immediately.

knowledge.fact: The DAS 2025 adult algorithm progresses to Plan D emergency front-of-neck airway after unsuccessful airway rescue and CICO recognition.
2025 guidance emphasises early decisive Plan D and a standardised vertical skin incision approach when appropriate.
Waveform capnography is required to confirm effective tracheal ventilation and is not interchangeable with chest rise alone.
Continuing oxygen delivery, teamwork and non-repetition of unsuccessful approaches remain essential during airway rescue.
Equipment, communication and technical practice are essential elements of airway rescue preparation.
Once a rescue airway is secured, ongoing monitoring and documentation are essential.

recall.think: Oxygenation failure after A, B and C: this is Plan D, not one more attempt.
recall.say: “CICO confirmed; activate eFONA and call for help.”
do: Stabilise larynx, perform controlled scalpel–bougie–tube access on the model and attach circuit.

numbers.meaning: No saturation threshold is needed once CICO is clinically declared; act immediately.

recall.trap: A tube in the neck without a CO₂ trace is not a confirmed airway.
recall.finish: Confirm sustained waveform capnography, secure the tube and hand over.

reveals.finding: You have a neck-training model, a scalpel, a bougie and a cuffed tracheal tube.
Saturation is falling despite rescue ventilation.

curveballs.prompt: After candidate identifies neck landmarks: “The membrane is difficult to feel.”
curveballs.safeAnswer: I will not make a blind stab at an uncertain point. I stabilise the larynx and use the DAS vertical skin incision approach to expose and identify the membrane.

curveballs.prompt: After tube is inserted: “There is no sustained end-tidal CO₂ trace.”
curveballs.safeAnswer: That is not confirmed ventilation. I immediately check the circuit, tube position and patency with the airway team; I do not assume the tube is intratracheal.
